entries.believed_open_because: Lagarias's 2010 survey documents the conjecture as unresolved since the 1930s: no termination proof and no closed form for the total stopping time exist, only density and stochastic partial results.
entries.progress_definition: Already probed: on 2026-08-14 the pipeline discovered two exact structures, sigma(2^k) = k on powers of two and the halving relation sigma(2n) = sigma(n) + 1, both holdout-confirmed. Progress = a new exact substructure law beyond those two, a proved statement about a restricted index family, or a certified refutation of a proposed law; a global closed form or termination claim is out of scope.
entries.source_citation: J. C. Lagarias (ed.), The Ultimate Challenge: The 3x+1 Problem, American Mathematical Society, 2010.
entries.statement: The total stopping time sigma(n) of the Collatz map (n -> n/2 for even n, n -> 3n+1 for odd n) is conjectured finite for every n >= 1; neither a termination proof nor a closed form for sigma(n) is known.

entries.believed_open_because: Elsholtz-Tao (2013) state the conjecture remains open in general: many residue classes are settled by parametric families and the statement is verified computationally to about 10^17, but no proof covers all n.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = a verified witness generator (x, y, z) for a residue class not covered by known parametric families, or a proved statement for such a class; exhaustive witness tables alone do not count.
entries.source_citation: C. Elsholtz and T. Tao, Counting the number of solutions to the Erdos-Straus equation on unit fractions, arXiv:1107.1010; J. Aust. Math. Soc. 94 (2013) 50-105.
entries.statement: For every integer n >= 2 there exist positive integers x, y, z with 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z.

entries.believed_open_because: Guy B6 records the Catalan-Dickson question as open and 276 as the smallest starting value whose aliquot sequence has never been shown bounded or unbounded despite thousands of computed terms.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = an exact invariant, growth law, or congruence structure of the computed trajectory that survives holdout, or a proved boundedness or unboundedness criterion applicable to 276; extending the raw trajectory is not progress.
entries.source_citation: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem B6 (aliquot sequences).
entries.statement: The aliquot sequence starting at 276, iterating s(n) = (sum of divisors of n) - n, is not known to terminate, enter a cycle, or diverge; its boundedness is unknown.

entries.believed_open_because: The Cramer conjecture literature (Cramer 1936; Granville 1995) documents that no closed form, polynomial or otherwise, is known for g(n), and even the conjectured (log p_n)^2 growth bound remains unproved.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = a certified refutation of any proposed closed form on holdout gaps (the expected outcome), or an exact law on a restricted index family that survives holdout; a global closed-form claim would contradict the cited literature and must be treated as a defect until externally verified.
entries.source_citation: H. Cramer, On the order of magnitude of the difference between consecutive prime numbers, Acta Arithmetica 2 (1936) 23-46; A. Granville, Harald Cramer and the distribution of prime numbers, Scandinavian Actuarial Journal 1995:1, 12-28.
entries.statement: No closed form is known for the prime gap sequence g(n) = p_(n+1) - p_n; Cramer's conjectured growth order g(n) = O((log p_n)^2) is unproved in both directions.

entries.believed_open_because: Not open: Euler proved the pattern in 1737. This entry is a rediscovery control; the pipeline must recover the known block structure from raw terms, and failure falsifies the method, not the mathematics.
entries.progress_definition: Control criterion: the pipeline rediscovers the (1, 2k, 1) block law from a prefix and confirms it on held-out terms. Rediscovery here is calibration evidence only and must never be reported as a novel discovery.
entries.source_citation: L. Euler, De fractionibus continuis dissertatio (presented 1737), Commentarii academiae scientiarum Petropolitanae 9 (1744) 98-137.
entries.statement: The simple continued fraction of e is [2; 1, 2, 1, 1, 4, 1, 1, 6, 1, 1, 8, ...]: after the leading 2, blocks (1, 2k, 1) for k = 1, 2, 3, ...

entries.believed_open_because: Not open mathematics: the generating recurrence is known to the sealing side and withheld from the discovery side. Openness here is operational (sealed holdout), not epistemic, and the entry is labeled synthetic accordingly.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = recovering a recurrence that reproduces every sealed holdout term exactly; the unseal receipt must record match or mismatch against the withheld generator. A mismatch is a valid sealed negative.
entries.source_citation: docs/CONTINUOUS_DISCOVERY_ROADMAP.md, Track A, item A2 (problem intake queue): internal synthetic sealed-holdout specification.
entries.statement: A synthetic sealed world: terms generated by an undisclosed Catalan-like polynomial-coefficient recurrence; the pipeline sees only the terms and must recover the recurrence.

entries.believed_open_because: McGaugh-Lelli-Schombert (2016) establish the radial acceleration relation empirically across 153 galaxies, but no derivation of a unique nu(y) from baryons alone is accepted; whether the relation reflects modified dynamics or dark-matter physics is unresolved.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = a nu(y) candidate that passes the full gate ladder (Newtonian limit, flatness, BTFR slope, positivity) beyond the 1,129,900,996-candidate GPU screen receipted at runs/gpu-baryonic-screen/billion-v1.json, and then survives the sealed validation ladder; per-galaxy free parameters are inadmissible.
entries.source_citation: S. S. McGaugh, F. Lelli, J. M. Schombert, Radial Acceleration Relation in Rotationally Supported Galaxies, Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 201101 (2016).
entries.statement: Find a universal law nu(y) mapping the baryonic gravitational acceleration g_bar to the observed acceleration g_obs = nu(g_bar/a0) * g_bar that reproduces flat outer rotation curves and the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation from baryons alone.

entries.believed_open_because: Brouwer et al. (2021) extend the radial acceleration relation about two decades lower in acceleration using lensing and show current data cannot decide between modified-gravity and cold-dark-matter explanations; no single law is established across both the dynamical and lensing regimes.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = a sealed consistency verdict: the surviving rotation-law candidate evaluated against the lensing relation with zero refitted parameters, recorded as an exact pass or an exact failure. A sealed failure is a valid outcome.
entries.source_citation: M. M. Brouwer et al., The weak lensing radial acceleration relation: Constraining modified gravity and cold dark matter theories with KiDS-1000, Astron. Astrophys. 650, A113 (2021).
entries.statement: Any universal acceleration law fitted to rotation-curve dynamics must, with no new freedom, also match the weak galaxy-galaxy lensing radial acceleration relation measured around isolated galaxies.

entries.believed_open_because: Sanders (1999) documents the residual factor ~2 mass discrepancy in clusters under MOND, and the subsequent literature has not produced a baryons-only law that fits both galaxies and clusters.
entries.progress_definition: Expected outcome is a sealed negative: candidate laws that pass the galaxy gates are evaluated on cluster mass data and the underprediction is receipted exactly. Progress = that sealed verdict, or a law family that measurably narrows the factor-2 gap without per-cluster freedom.
entries.source_citation: R. H. Sanders, The Virial Discrepancy in Clusters of Galaxies in the Context of Modified Newtonian Dynamics, Astrophys. J. 512, L23 (1999).
entries.statement: MOND-like acceleration laws that fit galaxy rotation curves underpredict the dynamical mass of galaxy clusters by roughly a factor of two; no baryons-only law is known to close the gap.

entries.believed_open_because: Not a named open problem: openness is internal. B3-surviving monotonicity and sign conjectures currently outnumber what the bounded proof templates can certify, so each uncertified family is open relative to this system's kernel-checked coverage.
entries.progress_definition: Progress = an increase in the count of B3-surviving quantified inequality families with kernel-checked proofs, receipted per family; a family whose proof search fails must be receipted as open with the failing goal recorded.
entries.source_citation: docs/CONTINUOUS_DISCOVERY_ROADMAP.md, Track B, together with src/sigma_theory_compiler/quantified_inequality_proofs.py and src/sigma_theory_compiler/lemma_decomposition.py (internal target).
entries.statement: Automatically prove, over Nat, the monotonicity and sign conjecture families that survive B3 holdout screening, via quantified inequality proof templates and lemma decomposition.

entries.believed_open_because: OEIS A023108 marks 196's membership as conjectural only: VanLandingham's p196.org search passed 300 million digits with no palindrome and later distributed continuations passed one billion digits, yet as of 2026 no proof exists in base 10 that any starting value never reaches a palindrome.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish exact range facts only: that no palindrome occurs within a declared iteration budget, exact digit-growth data for the computed trajectory, and B3 holdout verdicts on digit-length rows. It cannot establish that 196 is Lychrel; a termination claim must carry the exact palindrome witness. Budgets far below the p196.org records make this a mechanism receipt.
entries.source_citation: OEIS A023108 (numbers whose base-10 reverse-and-add trajectory apparently never reaches a palindrome); W. VanLandingham, p196.org record computations of the 196 trajectory (no palindrome through hundreds of millions of digits).
entries.statement: Does repeated reverse-and-add in base 10 starting from 196 ever produce a palindrome? No palindrome is known and no proof of non-termination exists; 196 is the smallest candidate Lychrel number.

entries.believed_open_because: Berndt-Galway (2000) verified computationally that no further solution has n <= 10^9, and as of 2026 the problem remains open: finiteness of solutions is known only conditionally (Overholt, under the abc conjecture).
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that within a declared exact-arithmetic range the only solutions are n = 4, 5, 7, each carried with its exact square-root witness. Any sweep below the Berndt-Galway bound of 10^9 is a mechanism receipt and adds no new bound; it cannot establish finiteness.
entries.source_citation: H. Brocard, Question 166, Nouvelle Correspondance Mathematique 2 (1876) 287, and Question 1532, Nouvelles Annales de Mathematiques (3) 4 (1885) 391; S. Ramanujan, Question 469, J. Indian Math. Soc. 5 (1913) 59; B. C. Berndt and W. F. Galway, On the Brocard-Ramanujan diophantine equation n! + 1 = m^2, Ramanujan J. 4 (2000) 41-42.
entries.statement: Brocard's problem: find all integers n with n! + 1 = m^2. Only n = 4, 5, 7 (m = 5, 11, 71) are known; whether any other solution exists is open.

entries.believed_open_because: Moser (1953) proved any further solution is astronomically large, and Gallot-Moree-Zudilin (2011) raised the bound to m > 10^(10^9) using continued fractions of log 2; as of 2026 no impossibility proof is known.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that a declared trivial (m, k) range contains only the known solution (k, m) = (1, 3), verified with exact integer power sums. The literature bound m > 10^(10^9) is unreachable by any sweep, so every sweep here is a mechanism receipt; range absence proves nothing beyond the range.
entries.source_citation: L. Moser, On the diophantine equation 1^n + 2^n + ... + (m-1)^n = m^n, Scripta Math. 19 (1953) 84-88; Y. Gallot, P. Moree, W. Zudilin, The Erdos-Moser equation 1^k + 2^k + ... + (m-1)^k = m^k revisited using continued fractions, Math. Comp. 80 (2011) 1221-1237.
entries.statement: The Erdos-Moser equation 1^k + 2^k + ... + (m-1)^k = m^k with k >= 1: the only known solution is 1 + 2 = 3 (k = 1, m = 3), and Moser's conjecture is that no other solution exists.

entries.believed_open_because: Guy B37 records the problem as open; Cohen-Hagis (1980) proved any composite counterexample has at least 14 distinct prime factors and exceeds 10^20, and as of 2026 neither a counterexample nor an impossibility proof is known.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that no composite n in a declared range satisfies phi(n) | n - 1, with a sieved totient table screened vectorially and every candidate re-verified exactly on CPU, plus the sanity fact that every prime in range passes. Ranges below the Cohen-Hagis bound of 10^20 make this a mechanism receipt.
entries.source_citation: D. H. Lehmer, On Euler's totient function, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 38 (1932) 745-751; R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem B37; G. L. Cohen and P. Hagis Jr., On the number of prime factors of n if phi(n) | n - 1, Nieuw Arch. Wisk. (3) 28 (1980) 177-185.
entries.statement: Lehmer's totient problem: does any composite n satisfy phi(n) | n - 1? Every prime does; no composite example is known, and Lehmer asked whether none exists.

entries.believed_open_because: Borwein-Borwein-Borwein-Girgensohn (1996) proved any composite counterexample must be squarefree, simultaneously a Giuga number and a Carmichael number, and must have more than 13800 digits; as of 2026 the conjecture remains open.

machine_form.equation: sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) = -1 (mod n) with n composite

entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that no composite n in a declared range satisfies the congruence, screened by the exact prime-factor criterion of Borwein et al. (1996) and cross-checked by direct modular power sums on an exhaustive subrange, with any screen survivor settled by the direct sum. Ranges below the 13800-digit literature bound are mechanism receipts.
entries.source_citation: G. Giuga, Su una presumibile proprieta caratteristica dei numeri primi, Ist. Lombardo Sci. Lett. Rend. Cl. Sci. Mat. Nat. (3) 83 (1950) 511-528; D. Borwein, J. M. Borwein, P. B. Borwein, R. Girgensohn, Giuga's conjecture on primality, Amer. Math. Monthly 103 (1996) 40-50.
entries.statement: Giuga's conjecture: n >= 2 is prime if and only if sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) = -1 (mod n). The forward direction is classical; no composite n satisfying the congruence is known.

entries.believed_open_because: Ochem-Rao (2012) proved any odd perfect number exceeds 10^1500 and has at least 101 prime factors counted with multiplicity; as of 2026 no example and no impossibility proof exist, and Guy B1 documents the question as open.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that no odd n in a declared range satisfies sigma(n) = 2n, using a segmented divisor-sum sieve screened vectorially with exact CPU re-verification of candidates, sanity-anchored on the even perfect numbers the same sieve must find. Any feasible range sits far below the Ochem-Rao bound of 10^1500, so this lane is a mechanism receipt by construction.
entries.source_citation: P. Ochem and M. Rao, Odd perfect numbers are greater than 10^1500, Math. Comp. 81 (2012) 1869-1877; R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem B1.
entries.statement: Does an odd perfect number exist, i.e. an odd n with sigma(n) = 2n? None is known; existence and impossibility are both unproved.

entries.believed_open_because: Guy B10 records the question as open: the reduction of odd untouchables to a strengthened Goldbach statement is itself unproved, and Erdos (1973) proved that untouchable numbers have positive lower density, so they do not thin out. Open as of 2026.

machine_form.equation: s(m) = sigma(m) - m = n has no solution m

entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish the exact list of untouchable numbers up to a declared bound L - computed by an exhaustive aliquot-preimage argument whose completeness bound (composite preimages with three or more prime factors satisfy m <= L^(3/2), with prime, prime-square, and semiprime preimages enumerated directly) is stated in the receipt - and in particular which odd values occur. Enumeration to any bound leaves the conjecture open.
entries.source_citation: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem B10 (untouchable numbers); P. Erdos, Uber die Zahlen der Form sigma(n) - n und n - phi(n), Elem. Math. 28 (1973) 83-86.
entries.statement: Untouchable numbers are those not of the form s(m) = sigma(m) - m for any m. Is 5 the only odd untouchable number? This would follow if every even number at least 8 were a sum of two distinct primes, a strengthening of Goldbach's conjecture.

entries.believed_open_because: Zhang (2014) proved some even gap below 7 x 10^7 occurs infinitely often and Polymath8b (2014) lowered the proven gap to 246, but the gap-2 case remains unproved as of 2026; Guy A8 documents the conjecture's open status.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish exact pi_2(10^k) values from a sieve, cross-checked against OEIS A007508, plus which typed conjectures over those rows survive or are refuted on holdout. No finite table can decide infinitude; growth-law survivors remain conjectures with proved=false, and counts below published tables are mechanism facts.
entries.source_citation: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem A8; Y. Zhang, Bounded gaps between primes, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014) 1121-1174; D. H. J. Polymath, Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes, Res. Math. Sci. 1 (2014), article 12; OEIS A007508.
entries.statement: Are there infinitely many primes p with p + 2 also prime? The machine form tracks the twin-prime counting function pi_2(10^k), the number of primes p <= 10^k with p + 2 prime.

entries.believed_open_because: Odlyzko (1993) verified the conjecture for the first 3.4 x 10^11 difference rows (working from primes below 10^13) and gave heuristic support, but no proof is known as of 2026; Guy A10 lists it as open and records that Proth's 1878 claimed proof was faulty.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish that every computed difference row in a declared budget has leading term 1 - an exact range fact far below Odlyzko's 3.4 x 10^11 rows, hence a mechanism receipt - and record which typed conjectures on the leading-term rows survive holdout. Survival restates the conjecture as a conjecture; it proves nothing.
entries.source_citation: N. L. Gilbreath's 1958 conjecture, documented in R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed., Springer, 2004, problem A10; A. M. Odlyzko, Iterated absolute values of differences of consecutive primes, Math. Comp. 61 (1993) 373-380.
entries.statement: Gilbreath's conjecture: iterate absolute differences on the sequence of primes; after the row of primes itself, every row begins with 1.

entries.believed_open_because: Steinerberger (2017) found empirically a constant alpha ~ 2.5714 with cos(alpha a_n) < 0 for all computed terms except 2, 3, 47, 69, but neither this signal, a closed form, nor positive density has been proved as of 2026; OEIS A002858 records the structure questions as open.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish exact initial terms of U(1,2) under the declared budget and record verbatim which typed conjectures (closed forms, recurrences, monotonicity, sign) survive or are refuted on holdout. The expected outcome is refutation of every closed-form lane; survivors are conjectures only, and density claims are out of scope.
entries.source_citation: S. M. Ulam, Problems in Modern Mathematics, Science Editions, Wiley, New York, 1964, p. xi; S. Steinerberger, A hidden signal in the Ulam sequence, Experimental Mathematics 26 (2017) 460-467; OEIS A002858.
entries.statement: The Ulam sequence U(1,2) = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11, ... (each subsequent term is the smallest integer with exactly one representation as a sum of two distinct earlier terms) has no known closed form; its apparent positive density near 0.074 and its quasi-periodic structure are unproved.

entries.believed_open_because: The OEIS A005132 entry (as of 2026) records that extended computations - reported in the entry at scales far beyond 10^15 terms using compressed representations - have not reached 852655, and no proof of full coverage or of permanent omission of any value exists. The conjectural status is documented there, not inferred here.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish, for a declared step budget, the exact smallest positive integer not yet reached, the maximum value reached, and exact coverage counts. It cannot establish coverage or permanent omission of any value; budgets far below the searches reported in A005132 make this a mechanism receipt.
entries.source_citation: OEIS A005132 (Recaman's sequence), entry and comments by N. J. A. Sloane and contributors; the entry's computational reports document 852655 as the smallest value not known to appear, unreached in extended searches.
entries.statement: Does Recaman's sequence a(0) = 0, a(n) = a(n-1) - n if that is positive and not already in the sequence, else a(n-1) + n, contain every positive integer? OEIS A005132 records this as an open question.

entries.believed_open_because: Singmaster (1971) proved the multiplicity is O(log t) and conjectured it is O(1); Kane (2007) improved the bound to O(log t log log log t / (log log t)^3), still unbounded, and as of 2026 no absolute bound is proved and no t with multiplicity exceeding 8 is known.
entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish exact multiplicity counts N(t) for all t up to a declared bound, including the maximum observed multiplicity and every t attaining at least 6, plus holdout verdicts for typed conjectures over initial multiplicity rows. A bounded maximum in range is a range fact; it cannot establish the conjectured universal bound.
entries.source_citation: D. Singmaster, How often does an integer occur as a binomial coefficient?, Amer. Math. Monthly 78 (1971) 385-386; D. M. Kane, Improved bounds on the number of ways of expressing t as a binomial coefficient, Integers 7 (2007), article A53.
entries.statement: Singmaster's conjecture: the number of times any integer t > 1 appears as a binomial coefficient C(n, k) is bounded by an absolute constant. The largest known multiplicity is 8, attained by 3003.

entries.believed_open_because: Mauldin (1997) posed the conjecture as open with a prize attached, and as of 2026 the AMS-administered $1,000,000 Beal Prize remains unclaimed. Norvig's computational search notes report finding no counterexample in the boxes he searched (bases to 250,000 with exponents to 1,000, and bases to 1,000 with exponents to 250,000); published partial results settle only special exponent triples.

machine_form.equation: A^x + B^y = C^z with x >= 3, y >= 3, z >= 3

entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish, with exact integer confirmation of every screened near-hit, that a declared finite box (bases A, B <= Nb, exponents 3 <= x, y, z <= ze) contains no coprime solution, while known gcd > 1 families such as 3^3 + 6^3 = 3^5 must be rediscovered and labeled as controls. Any feasible box lies inside the documented search landscape, so every sweep is a mechanism receipt; a confirmed coprime solution is a counterexample candidate requiring independent exact re-verification and a loud claims flag, never a silent record.
entries.source_citation: R. D. Mauldin, A generalization of Fermat's Last Theorem: the Beal conjecture and prize problem, Notices Amer. Math. Soc. 44 (1997) 1436-1437; AMS Beal Prize (funded by D. A. Beal, raised to $1,000,000 in 2013); P. Norvig, Beal's conjecture: a search for counterexamples, norvig.com (computational search notes).
entries.statement: The Beal conjecture: if A^x + B^y = C^z with A, B, C, x, y, z positive integers and x, y, z >= 3, then A, B, and C have a common prime factor. Fermat's Last Theorem is the special case x = y = z; a verified coprime solution would refute the conjecture.

entries.believed_open_because: Darmon-Granville (1995) proved finiteness for each fixed exponent triple (p, q, r) with 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1, but finiteness over all exponent triples remains unproved as of 2026; exactly ten solutions are known and no new solution has been reported since the computational searches of the 1990s.

machine_form.equation: x^p + y^q = z^r with gcd(x, y) = 1 and 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1

entries.progress_definition: A receipt can establish the complete list of coprime solutions inside a declared finite box (bases x, y <= Nb, exponents p, q <= pe and r <= re subject to 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1) with exact integer confirmation of every screened near-hit, and must rediscover every builtin known solution reachable in the box, labeled as such. A confirmed solution absent from the builtin table is recorded as new-to-table with a prior-art note and no novelty claim. No finite box bears on finiteness.
entries.source_citation: H. Darmon and A. Granville, On the equations z^m = F(x, y) and Ax^p + By^q = Cz^r, Bull. London Math. Soc. 27 (1995) 513-543; B. Poonen, E. F. Schaefer, M. Stoll, Twists of X(7) and primitive solutions to x^2 + y^3 = z^7, Duke Math. J. 137 (2007) 103-158 (records the standard list of the ten known solutions).
entries.statement: The Fermat-Catalan conjecture: the equation x^p + y^q = z^r with x, y, z coprime positive integers and exponents satisfying 1/p + 1/q + 1/r < 1 has only finitely many solutions, counting the powers x^p, y^q, z^r. Exactly ten solutions are known, beginning 1^m + 2^3 = 3^2, 2^5 + 7^2 = 3^4, 7^3 + 13^2 = 2^9, 2^7 + 17^3 = 71^2, and 3^5 + 11^4 = 122^2.

entries.believed_open_because: Elsholtz-Tao (2013) state the conjecture remains open in general, and Salez (2014) reports computational verification of all n up to 10^17 without a proof; as of 2026 no argument covers all n, so every bounded witness sweep below that bound is a mechanism receipt.

machine_form.equation: 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z with x <= y <= z (bounded witness sweep)

entries.progress_definition: Cross-reference: re-enters queue entry erdos_straus in sweeper form with a distinct id; progress on the mathematics is defined by the original entry. A receipt can establish NO_UNSOLVABLE_N_IN_RANGE for a declared range 2 <= n <= n_max with every stored witness verified in exact rational arithmetic, storing per-class witness samples and extremal minimal-x witnesses rather than full witness tables. Any feasible range sits below the verified 10^17 and adds no new bound.
entries.source_citation: C. Elsholtz and T. Tao, Counting the number of solutions to the Erdos-Straus equation on unit fractions, arXiv:1107.1010; J. Aust. Math. Soc. 94 (2013) 50-105; S. E. Salez, The Erdos-Straus conjecture: New modular equations and checking up to N = 10^17, arXiv:1406.6307 (2014).
entries.statement: Sweeper-form re-entry of queue entry erdos_straus (v1): for every integer n >= 2 there exist positive integers x <= y <= z with 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z. This entry carries the bounded witness-sweep parameterization (residue-class parametric witnesses plus exact search on the hard class n = 1 mod 12) and claims no separate mathematical target beyond the original entry.
